A former First Mayor of Hamburg and finance minister, this Social Democrat succeeded Angela Merkel as Germany's leader, serving as chancellor from 2021 to 2025 — who is he?
Olaf Scholz: Chancellor of Germany from 2021 to 2025. Olaf Scholz (born 14 June 1958) is a German politician who served as the chancellor of Germany from 2021 to 2025.

This 19th-century South American conflict was the deadliest interstate struggle in Latin American history, pitting one nation against an allied trio of neighboring countries from 1864 to 1870 — which conflict?
Paraguayan War: Major international war in South America (1864–1870)
A close ally of Robespierre, this French revolutionary chose suicide over arrest when authorities stormed the Hôtel de Ville during the coup of 9–10 Thermidor — who was he?
Born in London to a Ugandan-Indian family, this Conservative MP for Witham served as Home Secretary from 2019 to 2022 before becoming Shadow Foreign Secretary — who is she?

As Sweden's special envoy in Budapest in 1944 he saved thousands of Jews with protective passports and "Swedish territory" safe houses, then vanished in 1945 after Soviet SMERSH agents detained him — who was this humanitarian diplomat?
Raoul Wallenberg: Swedish diplomat and humanitarian (1912–1945). Raoul Wallenberg (4 August 1912 – disappeared 17 January 1945) was a Swedish architect, businessman, diplomat, and humanitarian.
The longest-serving prime minister in Slovak history, he has led the country across four separate terms since founding his left-wing party in 1999 — who is he?
Prince Albert Victor, Duke of Clarence and Avondale
Robert Fico: Prime Minister of Slovakia (2006–2010, 2012–2018, 2023–present)
After serving as Prime Minister of Kuwait from 1978 to 2006, this royal briefly became Emir for just nine days before abdicating — who is he?
Saad Al-Salim Al-Sabah: Emir of Kuwait in 2006.
Anointed by the prophet Samuel as the first king of a newly unified Israelite kingdom, he died falling on his own sword after defeat by the Philistines at Mount Gilboa — who was he?
Saul: Biblical figure and Israelite monarch.
This Indian politician served four terms as Chief Minister of Maharashtra and founded a new party in 1999 after splitting from the Indian National Congress — who is he?
Sharad Pawar: Indian politician. Sharadchandra Govindrao Pawar (born 12 December 1940) is an Indian politician who has served as a Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha since 2014.

In just 96 hours of 1967, Israel captured the West Bank, Gaza, the Sinai Peninsula, and the Golan Heights from three Arab nations—a lightning campaign that reshaped the Middle East. What is this brief but transformative war called?
Six-Day War: 1967 war between Israel and Arab states.
This retired US Airways pilot safely ditched his disabled airliner on the Hudson River in January 2009 after a bird strike knocked out both engines, saving all 155 aboard — who is he?
Sully Sullenberger: American pilot and diplomat (born 1951)
Born Namgyal Wangdi, this Sherpa mountaineer stood atop Mount Everest alongside Edmund Hillary in 1953, becoming one of the first two confirmed to reach the summit — who is he?

The third son of Japan's founding Edo-period shōgun, this samurai ruled as the second shōgun of that dynasty from 1605 until his 1623 abdication, and became grandfather to Empress Meishō — who was he?
Tokugawa Hidetada: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military ruler of Japan from 1605 to 1623.
With Merlin's magic making him look like his rival Gorlois, this legendary British king slept with Lady Igraine and fathered a certain 'once and future king' — who was he?
Uther Pendragon: Father of King Arthur in Arthurian legend.
Credited with coining the phrase 'sovereign democracy' while shaping Kremlin strategy for over a decade, this close Putin aide earned the nickname 'grey cardinal' — who is he?
As chief of the OKW, this German field marshal signed the criminal orders that fed countless war crimes — and was so deferential to Hitler that colleagues reviled him. Who was he?
Founded in London in 1844 by George Williams to promote 'muscular Christianity,' this youth organization now serves over 64 million people worldwide?
YMCA: Worldwide youth organization. YMCA is a worldwide youth organization based in Vernier, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland, with more than 64 million beneficiaries in 120 countries.
Emerging in late-19th-century Europe in reaction to antisemitism and led by Theodor Herzl, this nationalist movement sought a Jewish homeland in Palestine — what is it?
Zionism: Jewish nationalist movement. The arrival of Zionist settlers in Palestine during this period is widely seen as marking the start of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict.
Who among these was born first?
Soichiro Honda (born 1906) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Jan Hus (born 1369) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
Louis Slotin is a physicist. Louis Alexander Slotin ( SLOHT-in; 1 December 1910 – 30 May 1946) was a Canadian physicist and chemist who took part in the Manhattan Project.
Which of these is a chemist?
Elizabeth Rona is a chemist. Elizabeth Rona (20 March 1890 – 27 July 1981) was a Hungarian nuclear chemist, known for her work with radioactive isotopes.
What is the atomic number of Tennessine?
Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
What is the atomic number of Astatine?
Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
In what year was Bill Wyman born?
Bill Wyman: William George Wyman (né Perks; born 24 October 1936) is an English musician who was the bassist of the rock band the Rolling Stones from 1962 to 1993.
In what year was Ferdinand Porsche born?
Ferdinand Porsche (3 September 1875 – 30 January 1951) was an Austrian-German automotive engineer and founder of the Porsche AG.
In what year did Pythagoras die?
Pythagoras: Pythagoras of Samos (Ancient Greek: Πυθαγόρας; c. 570 – c. 495 BC) was an ancient Ionian Greek philosopher, polymath, and the eponymous founder of Pythagoreanism.
In what year did Richard Feynman die?
Richard Feynman: Richard Phillips Feynman (May 11, 1918 – February 15, 1988) was an American theoretical physicist.
In what year was Molybdenum discovered?
Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.
In what year was Titanium discovered?
Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.
Mikoyan MiG-27: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. It is based on the Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23 fighter aircraft, but optimised for air-to-ground attack.
In which country is Dassault Rafale based?
Dassault Rafale: France. Dassault built a technology demonstrator that first flew in July 1986 as part of an eight-year flight-test programme, paving the way for approval of the project.
Who is credited with discovering Technetium?
Technetium: Emilio G. Segrè. Technetium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tc and atomic number 43.
Who is credited with discovering Cell theory?
Who is credited with discovering Hydrazine?
Hydrazine: Hermann Emil Fischer. Hydrazine is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula N2H4.
Sharing the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces, who became the first Muslim scientist to win a Nobel?
Abdus Salam (29 January 1926 - 21 November 1996) was a Pakistani theoretical physicist and Nobel laureate.

Born into a prominent Stockholm family, this fluent-in-six-languages inventor filed his first patent at 24 and went on to hold 355 in all, while owning the arms-and-engineering firm Bofors. Who was he?
Alfred Nobel (noh-BEL; 21 October 1833 - 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, inventor, engineer, and businessman.
This type of long-term arthritis causes inflammation where the spine meets the pelvis, with lower back pain as its hallmark symptom. What condition is it?
Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis from the disease spectrum of axial spondyloarthritis.

This German philosopher's 1818 masterwork describes the visible world as the manifestation of a blind, irrational underlying will, building on Kantian idealism while rejecting German idealism's optimism — who is he?
Arthur Schopenhauer (22 February 1788 - 21 September 1860) was a German philosopher and writer.
The first production aircraft of its type, this American military transport combines vertical takeoff and landing with long-range cruise performance—what is it?
Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey is an American multi-use, tiltrotor military transport and cargo aircraft with both vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) and short takeoff and landing (STOL) capabilities.
Recognised by South Africa's Kennel Union but not by the international federation, this large, muscular mastiff-type breed serves as a family guard dog — name it?
Boerboel is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
This English-like, compiled programming language was designed for business use and remains widely used today to maintain legacy mainframe systems in banking and government — what language is it?
COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which metabolic process is the polar opposite of anabolism, breaking large molecules such as proteins and lipids down into monomers while releasing energy, some of it lost as heat?
Catabolism is the set of metabolic pathways that breaks down molecules into smaller units that are either oxidized to release energy or used in other anabolic reactions.
The first element in group 6, it lends its name to the shiny plating on car bumpers and, mixed into steel, makes it stainless. Which steely-grey metal is it?
Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
Known in the US as 'konk,' this sea snail's family includes so-called 'true' species identified by their long spires — what is it?
Conch is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
This term describes all the material inside a cell's outer membrane, excluding the nucleus (in cells that have one) — its main components include a gel-like fluid called the cytosol. What is it?
Cytoplasm is all the material within a eukaryotic or prokaryotic cell, enclosed by the cell membrane, including the organelles and excluding the nucleus in eukaryotic cells.

Bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba, Argentina, for hunting big game like wild boar and pumas, this large mastiff-type dog breed traces its ancestry partly to a now-extinct fighting dog — name the breed?
Dogo Argentino (plural Dogos Argentinos) is an Argentine breed of large dog of mastiff type.

This German chess champion — also a mathematician and philosopher — held the world title for 27 years, the longest reign ever, and was famed for a 'psychological' approach said to unsettle opponents. Who was he?
Emanuel Lasker (German; December 24, 1868 - January 11, 1941) was a German chess player, mathematician, and philosopher.
First confirmed around a pulsar in 1992, this astronomical term describes any planet located outside our own solar system — over 6,300 have now been confirmed — what is it called?
Exoplanet is a planet outside the Solar System. The first confirmed detection of an exoplanet was in 1992 around a pulsar, and the first detection around a main-sequence star was in 1995.
This American political scientist argued in a controversial 1992 book that the spread of liberal democracy and free markets might be the final form of human government — who is he?
Francis Fukuyama (born October 27, 1952) is an American political scientist, political economist, and international relations scholar.
Often called the 'silent thief of sight' because it creeps up slowly, this group of eye diseases damages the optic nerve and is closely tied to raised pressure inside the eye — what is it?
Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that can lead to damage of the optic nerve, which transmits visual information from the eye to the brain.
Named for a flattened, laterally extended head shape called a cephalofoil, with eyes placed at each end of the T, this family of sharks includes species mostly grouped in one genus — which sharks?

Hammerhead shark are a group of sharks that form the family Sphyrnidae, named for the unusual and distinctive form of their heads, which are flattened and laterally extended into a cephalofoil (a T-shape or "hammer").
This perennial root vegetable, a relative of mustard, wasabi, broccoli, and cabbage, is grated and used worldwide as a pungent spice and condiment — what plant is it?
Representing about three-quarters of circulating antibodies in humans, which type of antibody is released by plasma B cells?
Immunoglobulin G (IgG) is a type of antibody.
This German-American software engineer designed PayPal's real-time anti-fraud system, then co-founded a site whose very first video — "Me at the zoo" — he uploaded himself in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim (born October 28, 1979) is a German and American software engineer and internet entrepreneur.
In this crime drama, a motorcycle stunt rider turns to bank robbery to support his ex-lover and their newborn son, setting off a story spanning three linear timelines. What film is it?
Ketone is an organic compound with the structure RC(=O)R', where R and R' can be a variety of carbon-containing substituents.
Distinguished from its cousins the pikas by short furry tails and elongated ears and hind legs, this mammal family comprises over 70 species we commonly call rabbits and hares — which family?
Leporidae is the family of rabbits and hares (Lepus), containing over 70 species of extant mammals in all.
Serving under Chancellor Adenauer, this economist championed West Germany's postwar economic miracle before becoming chancellor himself in 1963 — who is he?
Ludwig Erhard (4 February 1897 - 5 May 1977) was a German politician and economist who served as the second chancellor of West Germany from 1963 until 1966.
The heaviest and largest members of the squirrel family, these 15 species of grazing ground-dwellers vanish each winter to hibernate underground — what are they?
Marmot are large ground squirrels in the genus Marmota, with 15 species living in Asia, Europe, and North America.
This Hungarian-American psychologist identified and named the highly focused, creativity-boosting mental state known as 'flow' — who is he?
Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi (29 September 1934 - 20 October 2021) was a Hungarian-American psychologist.
With somewhere between 66 and 70 species across nine subfamilies, this carnivore family stretches from tiny weasels all the way up to the wolverine. What is it?
Mustelidae (from Latin mustela, weasel) are a diverse family of carnivoran mammals, including weasels, badgers, otters, sea otters, polecats, martens, grisons and wolverines.
Element 102 honors the inventor of dynamite, and its short-lived isotope 255 — with a 3-minute half-life — is the one chemists actually prefer to work with. Which synthetic actinide is it?
Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.

This group of middle-ear inflammations includes a painful acute infection that makes young children tug at their ears, plus a quieter form defined by non-infectious fluid lingering for weeks. What is the condition?
Otitis media is a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear.
Recognized by a long beak and an enormous throat pouch used to drain water from scooped-up prey before swallowing, these large water birds come in eight living species worldwide — which birds?
Pelican (genus Pelecanus) are a genus of large water birds that make up the family Pelecanidae.

A perennial legume native to the Eastern Hemisphere, this crop is a staple across the Indian Subcontinent, Africa and the Caribbean despite a name that sounds more like a bird than a bean. What is it?
Pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) is a perennial legume from the family Fabaceae native to the Eastern Hemisphere.
Domesticated roughly 8,000 years ago in Southeast Asia, chickens are the most common example of this category of farmed birds — what's the term?
Poultry are domesticated birds kept by humans for the purpose of harvesting animal products such as meat, eggs or feathers.
Named partly for the Aztec feathered serpent god and partly for the designer of a tailless aircraft, this genus of giant pterosaur soared over Late Cretaceous North America — what is it?
Quetzalcoatlus is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur that lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in North America.

This interdisciplinary field studies and practices the design, construction, and operation of robots, typically combining a power source, mechanical structure, control circuitry, and software — what's the field called?
Robotics is the interdisciplinary study and practice of the design, construction, operation, and use of robots.
This condition gives the spine an irregular S- or C-shaped curve with a twist, and is often compared with kyphosis and lordosis — what is it?
Scoliosis (pl.: scolioses) is a medical condition in which the spine has an irregular curve in the coronal plane, associated with a rotational component.
About 0.01% of people are born with this condition, in which the heart typically ends up on the right side of the chest instead of the left — what is it?
Situs inversus is a congenital condition in which the major visceral organs are reversed or mirrored from their normal positions.

Held together by its own gravity, this luminous sphere of plasma is the type of object our Sun is, with roughly 4,000 of them visible to the naked eye on a clear night - what are these objects called?
Star is a luminous spheroid of plasma held together by self-gravity.

Named after a figure from Greek mythology condemned to eternal frustration, this hard, corrosion-resistant blue-gray metal, atomic number 73, is mined alongside the chemically similar niobium in the ore known as coltan. What element is this?
Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
The largest member of the genus Panthera and an apex predator of Asian forests, this big cat wears orange fur striped in mostly-vertical black — what is it?
Tiger (Panthera tigris) is a large cat and a member of the genus Panthera native to Asia.
With 92 protons and half-lives stretching up to 4.5 billion years, this radioactive metal is handy for dating the age of the Earth — which silvery-grey element?
Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.
Belonging mostly to one family of long-snouted beetles, this group includes bark beetles and grain-damaging pests despite some members lacking the trademark snout — what are they?
Weevil are beetles belonging to the superfamily Curculionoidea, known for their very long snouts.
The second asteroid ever discovered and likely a leftover protoplanet, this object is the third-largest in the asteroid belt by mass — about 79% the mass of Vesta — what is it?
2 Pallas: Third-largest asteroid. Pallas (minor-planet designation: 2 Pallas) is the third-largest asteroid in the Solar System by volume and mass.
Known for the fused bony 'boss' across its forehead, this large, notoriously unpredictable Sub-Saharan bovine has never been domesticated — what animal is it?
Defined by at least one carbon-carbon triple bond and traditionally nicknamed for its simplest member, ethyne (better known as acetylene) — which class of hydrocarbon is this?
Alkyne: Hydrocarbon compound containing one or more C≡C bonds.
Also called water boas, these semiaquatic South American snakes include the world's largest species by weight, a green-hued giant — which snakes?
Anaconda: Genus of snakes. Two to four extant and one extinct species are currently recognized, including one of the largest snakes in the world, E. murinus, the green anaconda.
Usually symptomless until it ruptures — causing sudden, severe abdominal or lower-back pain — this dangerous enlargement of the body's main artery is most common in the abdomen — what condition?
Aortic aneurysm: Excessive enlargement of the human aorta.

First catalogued in 1729 by an Italian priest who thought its spore-forming structures resembled a holy-water sprinkler, this genus of several hundred mold species takes its name from the Latin word for 'to sprinkle' — which genus?
Aspergillus: Genus of fungi. Aspergillus is a genus consisting of several hundred mold species found in various climates worldwide.
Named from a Greek word meaning 'heavy,' this soft silvery alkaline earth metal with atomic number 56 wasn't isolated until 1808 via electrolysis, decades after being identified — which element?
Barium: Chemical element with atomic number 56 (Ba)
This red-orange breakdown product of heme colors feces brown and urine pale yellow as it's further broken down in the body — which compound?
Bilirubin: Red pigment of the bile.
Modified from a 747-200B and nicknamed the 'Doomsday plane,' this USAF aircraft serves as a survivable airborne command post for the president during nuclear war — which aircraft?
Boeing E-4: US Air Force airborne command squadron aircraft.
Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and spread mainly through infected fleas, this illness produces swollen, painful lymph nodes nicknamed 'buboes' — what disease?
Bubonic plague: Human and animal disease.
This biological family includes wolves, foxes, jackals, and domestic dogs, ranging in size from the 6.6-foot gray wolf down to the tiny fennec fox — what is it called?
Canidae: Family of mammals. Canidae (from Latin, canis, "dog") is a biological family of caniform carnivorans, constituting a clade.

Derived from the amino acid tyrosine, this class of molecules includes adrenaline, noradrenaline, and dopamine, and drives the fight-or-flight response when released from the adrenal glands. What are they called?
Caused by a member of the herpesvirus family, this airborne illness usually starts on the chest, back, and face before the itchy little blisters scab over all over the body — what is it?
Its visible portion, the glans, is roughly the size of a pea yet packs over 10,000 nerve endings, making it the primary source of female sexual pleasure. What is this organ?
Clitoris: Erectile female sexual organ. In amniotes, the clitoris (KLIT-ər-iss or klih-TOR-iss; pl.: clitorises or clitorides) is a female sex organ.

This small, ground-nesting game bird has a call of three quick chirps repeated in succession, breeds across Europe, and winters in Africa and southern India — which species, often confused with a similar-sounding Japanese cousin?
Common quail: Species of bird. The common quail (Coturnix coturnix) or European quail is a small ground-nesting game bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae.

Ancient Greek, Chinese, and Indian cultures lacked a concept for this, seeing art as discovery rather than invention, while the Judeo-Christian-Islamic tradition later reserved it for God alone — what mental faculty is this?
Creativity: Forming something new and somehow valuable.
Also known as jimsonweed or devil's trumpet, this poisonous nightshade plant likely native to Central America has been used both in folk medicine and, unpleasantly, as a hallucinogen — which plant?
Datura stramonium: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.
Nicknamed the 'businessman's trip' in the 1960s for its rapid onset and short duration, which naturally occurring tryptamine hallucinogen has long been used as a ritual entheogen?
Of the 68 species bearing this name, only the Aquilinae are genetically "true" ones — the rest just qualify as any bird of prey big enough to hunt sizeable vertebrates; what's the common name?
Eagle: Large bird of prey. Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.
This branch of biology and medicine studies the glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream, governing everything from growth to mood and metabolism — what is it called?
Endocrinology: Branch of medicine pertaining to the endocrine system.
Commonly called spurge, this giant plant genus includes the popular Christmas poinsettia and a thorny succulent nicknamed 'crown of thorns' — which genus is it?
This genus of small-to-medium wildcats — ranging from the diminutive black-footed cat to the larger jungle cat — also includes humanity's domestic pet, the housecat — which genus?
Found at the end of the leg and typically featuring claws or nails, which weight-bearing body part enables locomotion in many vertebrates?
Foot: Anatomical structure found in vertebrates.
Native to Central Asia and a close relative of the onion, shallot, and leek, this bulbous Allium has been a seasoning and folk remedy known to Babylonians, Egyptians, and Romans alike — what is it?
Nicknamed creeping charlie and alehoof, this aromatic mint-family creeper is eaten as a salad green in some countries but reviled as an invasive lawn weed in North America — what plant is it?
Glechoma hederacea: Species of plant in the mint family. It is commonly known as ground-ivy, gill-over-the-ground, creeping charlie, alehoof, tunhoof, catsfoot, field balm, and run-away-robin.
Marketed under the brand name Mucinex, this expectorant medication has been used to loosen chest congestion since at least 1933 — what is it?
Guaifenesin: Expectorant medication. It may be used in combination with other medications.

First proposed as early as the 3rd century BC by Aristarchus of Samos, this astronomical model places the sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe. What is this superseded model called?
Heliocentrism: Sun-centered astronomical model. Historically, heliocentrism was opposed to geocentrism, which placed Earth at the center.
Nicknamed 'Hobbit,' this extinct species of small archaic humans stood about 1.1 meters tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago — which species?
Homo floresiensis: Extinct small human species found in Flores.
Distinct from a process that adds more cells, this one is an increase in the size of individual cells, like the uterus enlarging during pregnancy — what's it called?
Hypertrophy: Increase in the size of biological cells. Hypertrophy can lead to a relative increase in the volume of a tissue or organ, and contributes to the overall growth of an organism.
Practitioners of this medical specialty are called internists in North America but simply 'physicians' in Britain, and often juggle patients with complex, multi-system disease — what field is it?
Internal medicine: Medical specialty dealing with adult diseases.
A PayPal engineer who built its real-time anti-fraud system, he co-founded a famous video site and uploaded its very first clip, 'Me at the zoo,' back in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim: American entrepreneur and software engineer (born 1979)
This evergreen conifer in the cypress family has the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere. What is it?
Juniperus communis: Species of tree in the cypress family.
Nocturnal, owl-faced, and unable to fly, this endangered New Zealand bird holds the title of the world's heaviest parrot. What is it?
Kākāpō: Parrot endemic to New Zealand. It is the only parrot to have a polygynous lek breeding system.
Often called the last physicist to master every branch of the field, this Soviet scientist co-discovered the density matrix method and developed the theory of superfluidity — who is he?
Also called dragon's eye, this tropical fruit tree from the soapberry family produces fruit similar to lychee but with a milder aroma, and is native to Southeast Asia and southern China — what is it?
Longan: Species of tropical fruit-bearing tree.
Transmitted through the bite of infected Anopheles mosquitoes and caused by single-celled Plasmodium parasites, which disease's symptoms typically begin 10 to 15 days after infection?
Distinguished by its darker camouflage, conformal fuel tanks, and a two-seat cockpit, this all-weather multirole fighter first flew in 1986 for long-range interdiction missions — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: American all-weather multirole fighter aircraft.
First made in 1969 and approved for medical use in 1978, this selective beta blocker treats high blood pressure, angina, and helps prevent migraines — what is it called?
Metoprolol: Beta blocker medication. It is also used to prevent further heart problems after myocardial infarction and to prevent headaches in those with migraines.
Its dust-like, colored, fuzzy appearance on food comes from spores, and its branching network of hyphae — called a mycelium — counts as a single organism; what fungal structure is this?
Mold: Wooly, dust-like fungal structure or substance.
This symbiotic partnership between fungus and plant roots plays a crucial role in plant nutrition and soil chemistry — usually mutualistic, but sometimes parasitic. What's the association called?
Mycorrhiza: Fungus-plant symbiotic association. The term mycorrhiza refers to the role of the fungus in the plant's rhizosphere, the plant root system and its surroundings.

This silvery-white transition metal with a faint golden tinge resists corrosion thanks to a thin oxide layer, and in pure native form it's mostly found inside iron meteorites — which element, atomic number 28, is it?
Nickel: Chemical element with atomic number 28 (Ni)
First described by Linnaeus in 1758, this medium-sized spotted wild cat hunts armadillos and opossums at twilight across a range from the southwestern US to South America — what cat is it?
Ocelot: Species of wild cat. It is native to the southwestern United States, Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean islands of Trinidad and Margarita.

Triggered by a surge of luteinizing hormone near the midpoint of the menstrual cycle, this event sees the ovarian follicle rupture and release an egg — which breaks down in under a day if it isn't fertilized. What is it called?
Ovulation: Release of egg cells from the ovaries.
One of the 20th century's most prolific mathematicians, this Hungarian championed Ramsey theory and famously preferred cracking open problems to building grand theories — who was he?
Sold under the brand name Luminal, this WHO-recommended barbiturate treats epilepsy in children and can be given intravenously for status epilepticus — which drug?
Phenobarbital: Medication of the barbiturate type.
Injected by a mosquito's bite and multiplying first in the liver before invading red blood cells, this parasite genus is the cause of malaria — what is it?
Plasmodium: Genus of parasitic protists that can cause malaria.
Originating in Spain's Canary Islands, this large mastiff-type breed was historically used for guarding, herding sheep and cattle, and — legally until 1936 — dog fighting. Which breed?
Presa Canario: Spanish breed of dog. It originates in the Spanish autonomous community of the Canary Islands, and is found mostly in the islands of Gran Canaria and Tenerife.
This white-yellow-brown fluid forms at sites of infection, and when trapped in an enclosed tissue space, it creates what's known as an abscess — what is it called?
Pus: Fluid produced by inflammatory infection.

Named after a 19th-century British naturalist employed by the East India Company, this small deer species native to south-eastern China and Taiwan has also become an established wild population in the UK and Ireland — what is it?
Reeves's muntjac: Species of deer. It has also been introduced in the United Kingdom, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Japan.
Grown in South Africa's Fynbos biome, this caffeine-free herbal infusion has an earthy flavor similar to yerba mate and carries protected designation of origin status in the EU. What is it?
Rooibos: Species of plant in the family Fabaceae.

This Harvard political scientist coordinated security planning for Jimmy Carter's National Security Council, but he's best remembered for a 1993 theory arguing future wars would be fought between cultures rather than countries — who was he?
Samuel P. Huntington: American political scientist and academic (1927–2008)
This secretive Soviet chief designer built the rocket that launched the first satellite, the first animal in orbit, and the first human into space — who was he?
Lose your coiled shell entirely and you're called a slug; keep one big enough to retract into and you're this shelled gastropod instead — what creature?
Snail: Shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.
This rodent family includes tree-dwelling, ground-dwelling, and gliding members like chipmunks and prairie dogs, and traces its fossil record back to the Eocene epoch — which animal family?
Squirrel: Family of rodents. The squirrel family includes tree squirrels, ground squirrels (including chipmunks and prairie dogs, among others), and flying squirrels.
Designed by R. J. Mitchell with a distinctive elliptical wing and sunken rivets for minimal drag, this was the only British fighter kept in continuous production throughout World War II — what is it?
